mcpTools.summary: Delete every bookmark for the file being watched, or for the file named.

mcpTools.summary: Point a mouse trigger at an action.

mcpTools.name: mouse_reset
mcpTools.summary: Restore a mouse trigger to its default.

mcpTools.summary: Return the frame showing right now as an image, so you can see what is on screen.

mcpTools.summary: Read the 10-band equaliser: per-band gains in dB, the band centre frequencies they correspond to, the preamp, whether loudness normalisation is on, and the filter chain mpv is actually running.

mcpTools.name: equalizer_set
mcpTools.summary: Adjust the equaliser.

mcpTools.name: equalizer_preset
mcpTools.summary: Apply a named equaliser curve and switch the equaliser on.

mcpTools.name: equalizer_presets
mcpTools.summary: List the available equaliser presets with a description of what each is for and the curve it applies.

mcpTools.name: equalizer_reset
mcpTools.summary: Remove every audio filter: flat curve, no preamp, no normalisation.

mcpTools.name: pitch_correction
mcpTools.summary: Read or set whether changing playback speed keeps the original pitch.

mcpTools.name: window_mode
mcpTools.summary: Get or set the shape of the player window the user is looking at.

mcpTools.summary: Find files an older unflick left behind — on Windows, upgrading from v0.9 moved the install directory and stranded roughly half a gigabyte with no uninstall entry.

mcpTools.summary: Optical drives on this machine and whether each holds a DVD or Blu-ray, plus whether this build can play them at all.

mcpTools.name: session
mcpTools.summary: What the user was last watching and how far in — and, with action "restore", reopen it there.

mcpTools.summary: The last launch's startup timeline, phase by phase, in milliseconds from process start — process init, video pipeline, window shown, the launch file opening, React mounting, the control port.

mcpTools.name: dev_text
mcpTools.summary: Visible text of every element matching a selector, each with its index.

mcpTools.summary: Wait for an element to appear, or with `gone` for it to leave the page.
